the development and evaluation of streaming keyword spotting systems based on sequence-to-sequence RNN-T models, which are capable of detecting arbitrary keyword phrases, and which are competitive with a strong CTC based keyword-filler baseline system.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed biasing method is a promising technique for improving RNN-T based streaming keyword spotting.
the RNN-T model with the proposed bias training technique outperforms the baseline keyword-filler system.
our RNN-T based keyword spotting systems are able to outperform the CTC-based keyword filler systems, with the proposed bias technique further improving performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to build an end-to-end streaming keyword spotting system which outperforms the baseline CTC-based keyword-filler system.
the RNN-T is able to learn to predict keywords in the same way as it learns to predict any other sequence of subword units, and that this ability is enhanced by the biasing technique.
we show how to use sequence-to-sequence modeling to perform keyword spotting, and how to improve the performance of such systems by biasing the model towards a specific keyword.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RNN-T model, with its ability to jointly learn acoustic and language model information, can be used for a wide range of keyword spotting applications.
sequence-to-sequence systems are promising alternatives to traditional keyword spotting systems, and can be adapted for streaming keyword spotting with a simple, effective technique.
the RNN-T model can achieve comparable performance to the CTC baseline, while having the advantage of being trained end-to-end.
